9	---
10	SilverBullet uses three fonts, each picked separately in [[Workbench/Configuration]] under **Appearance**:
11	
12	* **Interface font**: menus, panels, the page title and the [[Workbench]].
13	* **Editor font**: the text of your pages.
14	* **Code font**: anything code-like: inline code, [[Markdown/Fenced Code Block|code blocks]], frontmatter and tables while you edit them, and `${...}` expressions while the cursor is in them. It should be a monospace font.
15	
16	Instead of using the [[Workbench/Configuration]] options, you can also set them in [[CONFIG]]:
17	
18	```lua
19	config.set("fonts.editor", "inter")
20	config.set("fonts.ui", "system-sans")
21	config.set("fonts.code", "ia-writer-mono")
22	```
23	
24	# Editor font size
25	**Editor font size**, also under **Appearance**, sets the size of page text in the editor, in pixels: 18 by default, from 10 to 48. Headings, code and list indents scale with it. A proportional font often looks smaller than a monospace one at the same size, so you may want to raise it after switching. In [[CONFIG]]:
26	
27	```lua
28	config.set("fonts.editorSize", 20)
29	```
30	
31	# Built-in fonts
32	These come with SilverBullet, or with your operating system, and work offline:
33	
34	* **iA Writer Mono** (`ia-writer-mono`): the default for all three.
35	* **Inter** (`inter`): a clear sans for the interface and the editor.
36	* **System sans**, **System serif** and **System mono** (`system-sans`, `system-serif`, `system-mono`): your operating system's own fonts, such as San Francisco on Apple devices and Segoe UI on Windows.
37	
38	# The default font
39	When a space doesn’t pick an interface or editor font, it uses the default font: in SilverBullet Server, the **Default font** in the dashboard's Server settings; in SilverBullet Desktop, **Font** under Advanced. The default font also sets the dashboard and sign-in pages.
40	
41	# Font libraries
42	Additional fonts can be distributed as [[Library|libraries]]. If you uninstall a font library while a space still uses its font, the interface and editor fall back to the default font.
43	
44	## Writing a font library
45	A font library is an ordinary [[Library]]: a page that adds its font to `fonts.available`, with the font files listed under `files` in its frontmatter so they're installed with it.

49	  name = "Literata",                   -- shown in Configuration
50	  family = "Literata, Georgia, serif", -- the CSS font-family, with fallbacks
51	  kind = "serif",                      -- sans, serif or mono
